reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces handling for HTTP 429 (Too many requests) status codes in the Adyen API client, raising an `Adyen::APIError` when encountered. It also adds comprehensive unit tests to validate this behavior across legacy, RFC 7807, and non-JSON response formats. The feedback suggests updating the multi-line block in the new tests to use `do...end` instead of curly braces `{...}` to adhere to the Ruby style guide.

Thank you @pcbeingused333 for your contribution 🎉 

The PR is fine, this is a good improvement. Please address the open Gemini comment so we can proceed and merge it

review_comments.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In accordance with the community Ruby style guide and for consistency with the rest of the test suite in this file, multi-line blocks should use `do...end` instead of curly braces `{...}`.

```ruby
        expect { client.checkout.payments_api.payments(request_body) }
          .to raise_error(Adyen::APIError) do |error|
            expect(error).to be_a(Adyen::AdyenError)
            expect(error.code).to eq(429)
            expect(error.msg).to eq(message)
            expect(error.response).to eq(response_body)
            expect(error.request[:reference]).to eq('test')
          end
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid `{...}` for multi-line blocks. Always use `do...end` for multi-line blocks. <sup>([link](/Adyen/adyen-ruby-api-library/blob/main/.gemini/styleguide.md))</sup>
</details>
